chapters.title: Chapter 2594 Joining the First Division
paragraphs: Yuan and Mei Xiaoyun stood calmly before Mei Feng in her office.
"How's everything so far?" she asked them, her gaze mostly on Yuan.
"Boring," Yuan answered without hesitation.
"Not surprising, considering you've just finished your classes."
"When is the ceremony? I thought it was supposed to happen after the classes," he then said.
"It will happen right before the others are sent to training. Although you won't need to participate in the training, you still need to be present for the ceremony."
"Why did you call us here?" Mei Xiaoyun asked.
"Are you in a rush to be somewhere?" Mei Feng remarked.
When Mei Xiaoyun fell silent, Mei Feng turned to look at Yuan and asked, "Have you decided which Division you want to join?"
"Whichever Division will help me rank up and gain credentials the fastest."

"In that case, you'd want to join the First Division. They are always the first to be considered for missions. Moreover, with your combat expertise, I also think it's the most benefiting place for you."
"The First Division it is, then."

"A quick warning. The soldiers of the First Division tend to be more arrogant and prideful than those of the other Divisions because of their abilities. Since you're both new and received a rapid promotion, you may run into some trouble during your first few months. Just don't let it bother you," Mei Feng warned.
"Are you asking me to ignore them?" Yuan remarked with a playful smile.
"To the best of your abilities," she nodded.

"You should also be aware that although I command the First through Fourth Divisions, not everyone under me will be friendly. Some of them are even aligned with General Gu, so it would be wise to avoid unnecessary conflicts whenever possible."
"I'll do my best, but if it comes down to it, I'll defend myself."
Mei Feng nodded before clarifying, "I'm not asking you to sit there and take it. I simply don't want you drawing any more attention than you already have."

Mei Feng then turned to Mei Xiaoyun. "I won't ask why you suddenly changed your mind about joining the military, but if you ever need anything, speak to Sergeant Quang or Sergeant Bing. They'll do their best to accommodate you."
Mei Xiaoyun narrowed her eyes slightly. "I don't want any special treatment."

"As much as I'd like to leave you alone, it doesn't change the fact that you're my daughter, and as long as you're in the military, there will always be people who try to take advantage of you—or use you to get to me. In a way, you're in even more danger than Yuan."
Mei Xiaoyun silently sighed at Mei Feng's words. Even without being told, she was already aware of her own situation.
"I considered removing you from training, but ultimately decided against it. However, if anything happens, I'll pull you out immediately. Understood?" Mei Feng said a moment later.
"I understand..."
"Now, back to you..." Mei Feng returned to looking at Yuan.
"After the ceremony tomorrow, come back here. I still have more things to tell you."
"I understand."
Yuan and Mei Xiaoyun were escorted back to their living quarters, where they remained for the rest of the day.
The following morning, they were escorted to a spacious area, where every new soldier received their insignia after swearing the military's creed.
As the highest rank of all the new soldiers, Yuan received his insignia last.
After receiving his insignia, Yuan had to place his hand into a portal machine.
<You have been enlisted into the military>
<You have been promoted to the rank of Corporal>
<Your Credential Rank has increased>
<Your status has updated>
[Name: Yuan]
[Cultivation: Ninth Level Fifth Ascension]
[Military Rank: Corporal]
[Physique: Inexhaustible Heavenly Refinement]
[Credential Rank: 4]
[Cultivation Speed: 6]
Once everyone had received their insignias, all of the soldiers except Yuan were ordered to form a formation and march to their new training grounds, where they would spend the next year.
"See you later," Yuan said to Mei Xiaoyun.
"See you in a year... if nothing happens between that time, that is," she said.
"Let's not jinx it." Yuan chuckled. "And I'm sure your mother will have someone watch over you during training, even if she didn't mention it."
Yuan remained until Mei Xiaoyun and the other soldiers vanished into the horizon.
"Let's go see General Mei again," Yuan said to Sergeant Bing and Sergeant Quang.
Some time later, Yuan stood before Mei Feng again.
"First and foremost, let me congratulate you on officially joining the military," she said to him as she retrieved a piece of paper, placing it on the desk before her.
"Once you sign this, you'll also officially join the First Division, as well as complete our contract. Any questions before you do?"
"I do, but I doubt you'll answer them even if I asked."
"If it's related to Gaia, I cannot answer them."
"Then can you tell me about the sirens and the underground city? It's the first thing I experienced after coming to this world, and I still have no idea why it happened."
"Sure, I can explain that, since it's something you should know at your rank, but only after you sign this."
Yuan signed the documents a moment later.
"Great. Now you're officially part of the First Division."
<Ding!>
<You have joined the First Division>
<You have fulfilled the conditions of your contract with Mei Feng>
"Now, about your question..."
"I'm sure you've already learned this during your class, but our world is in danger."
"Yes, but I was not given any details."
"Because it's for your safety. If this information is something we can reveal freely, we would've already done so long ago. Unfortunately, that is not the case."
"Is it because this information is harmful? That it could literally kill?" Yuan asked.
Mei Feng narrowed her eyes at such words, a look of surprise in them.
"Where did you learn this information?" she asked him in a wary tone.
Yuan shrugged and said, "I am dealing with something similar in my world."
He continued, "Since I am already in the loop, you might as well tell me everything."
"That's not how things work," she swiftly responded. "Even if you know the reason we cannot reveal such information, it doesn't change the fact that you don't qualify to learn it."
"And how does one qualify? Let me guess... through my Credential Rank.

Mei Feng nodded. "The credential system isn't merely used to measure an individual's clearance and trustworthiness. It also determines whether they're capable of handling the information. You have no idea how many people have died from learning something they weren't supposed to learn."
"If you say so," said Yuan. "Let's return to the subject. Why is this world in danger?"
"Because that's what Gaia told us."
"Gaia told you the world is in danger...?" Yuan raised his eyebrows, looking puzzled.
"So you've spoken to Gaia before?"
"Of course. What kind of question is that?" Mei Feng stared at him with a weird expression.
"How do you speak to Gaia?"
"I don't understand your question."
"It's exactly as it sounds. How do you speak to them? Through the system? In person?"
"Obviously, we speak to Gaia through the system. However, it's also possible to speak to them in person, albeit much rarer."
"Is Gaia... human?" Yuan swallowed nervously before asking.
"What else would they be? An animal?" Mei Feng shook her head at his bizarre questions.
'So a human created Gaia's System...?' Yuan thought to himself after learning this new information.
'No... It's also entirely possible that it's an Eternal disguised as a human. If I want to know the truth, I will have to meet them in person.'
"Then how does one meet Gaia?" he then asked.
"You don't... at least not in your current state. If you want to even have a chance of meeting Gaia, you'll need at least Credential Rank 8."
"What a pain in the ass," Yuan sighed out loud.
"Gaia is literally the most important individual in this world. There's no way we'd let you meet them just because you want to."
"Even though Gaia told me to find them?" Yuan asked.
"Huh?" Mei Feng's eyes widened at his words, looking baffled by it.
"You heard that right. Gaia asked me to find them through the system."
"Even if you say that, there's no proof. Moreover, if Gaia really wants to meet you, they would've summoned you already. Anyways, enough about this subject."
Mei Feng then said, "According to Gaia, this world will be under attack in the near future by powerful beings from beyond our sky."
Yuan narrowed his eyes, immediately connecting these beings to Eternals.
"How will they attack?" Yuan asked a moment later.
"They will invade our world and enslave us, using humans for their experiments."
"You don't look surprised," Mei Feng remarked, noticing Yuan's lack of reaction.
Most people who first learned of the prophecy reacted with shock or fear, but Yuan gave the impression that he already knew or had been expecting it.
"Should I be surprised?" Yuan shrugged before asking, "Did Gaia reveal when they will attack this world?"
"No... but it will happen soon." Mei Feng sighed.
"And when they attack, this entire world will be engulfed in flames, hence why we created the underground city."
"So the sirens and escaping underground... It's just a practice drill for when the real thing happens? I heard that it would sometimes last for years at a time."

"That's correct." Mei Feng confirmed. "When the real attack happens, we will likely spend decades, if not longer, underground at a time, so it's for the best that we start early and familiarize ourselves with such a lifestyle."

chapters.title: Chapter 2595 Gravity Room
paragraphs: "What about the soldiers? I can assume that we won't go underground like the civilians, right?" Yuan asked after learning the truth.
Mei Feng nodded and said, "Obviously. Who else will fight the invaders if not us? You'll experience it yourself soon, too. The training drill, that is."
"I can't wait." Yuan smiled.
"Anyway, let's get to the main reason I called you here today."
Mei Feng's expression suddenly turned serious.

"This may seem sudden, but I am going to give you a mission. I know you just joined, and most new soldiers don't receive their first mission until their second year in the military, but you want fast promotions, right?"
He nodded.
"Of course. What kind of mission is it?"
"Clearing trash outside the city."
"...Excuse me?" Yuan muttered, his eyebrows raised in a puzzled manner.
"It's not literal trash. You'll understand once you get there," Mei Feng said.
"Will I be doing this alone? I have never been outside the city."
"Of course not. You'll be going with a team—a squad consisting of soldiers that I trust. I am not stupid enough to send you on your first mission alone."
"When do I start?"
"Next week. In the meantime, you can do whatever you want."
"I understand."
"If you have any more questions, you can ask them after the mission."
Yuan left her office shortly after.
As he was being escorted back to his living quarters, Yuan asked the Sergeants, "What do soldiers typically do on a daily basis?"
"We train," Sergeant Quang replied.
"What sort of training?"
"It'd be easier to show you. Want to take a look?"
"Let's."
Instead of returning to the living quarters, Yuan was escorted to the military building.
Once inside, they led him to the training area.
"You can find all of the training facilities here. It offers numerous training programs, ranging from combat proficiency to physical conditioning. Take this room, for example...
Sergeant Quang stopped in front of a room that had the words 'Gravity Room' engraved on top of the entrance.
"This is the Gravity Room, where you can temper your body under increased gravity. Want to give it a try?"
"Might as well, since we're already here."
Yuan followed Sergeant Quang into the room while Sergeant Bing waited outside.
Inside was a long hallway lined with numbered doors on either side. Some of these numbers emitted a green glow, while others glowed red.
"Any of the green rooms are available. The red ones are occupied."
Sergeant Quang gave him a quick rundown.
They entered the closest available room, number 17, a moment later.
The room was surprisingly spacious. At its center stood a mechanical pillar equipped with a screen and several buttons.
"You can adjust the gravity with that device, but it can also be voice-controlled. For example..."
"System, increase the gravity by one level."
The next moment, Yuan felt the atmosphere in the room shift as the weight pressing down on his body doubled.
"Each level doubles the gravity. In other words, level two subjects you to four times the normal gravity."
"Pretty neat. How many levels does it go up to?"
"Twenty levels."
"So a little over a million times normal gravity, huh?" Yuan muttered.
"What's the highest level anyone has reached?"
"Level 12, so about four thousand times normal gravity."
"What's your limit?" Yuan then asked.
"My limit is level 6."
"In that case... System, set gravity to level 5."
The gravity slowly increased, eventually reaching 32 times the normal gravity.
"Not bad..." Yuan muttered, looking completely fine, as if the increased gravity was not affecting him in the slightest.
"You... what rank is your physique at?" Sergeant Quang stared at him with wide eyes.
"Inexhaustible."
"The same physique rank as me? Yet, you can withstand level 5 much more easily than me." Sergeant Quang sighed.
"How about it? Want to try level 6?"
"Sure."
"System, set gravity to level 6."
The gravity doubled almost instantly, reaching 64 times the normal gravity.
Sergeant Quang immediately started sweating profusely, his knees bent as if struggling to withstand the increased gravity.
Meanwhile, Yuan's legs remained straight, looking fine even under the new gravity.
Seeing this, Sergeant Quang couldn't help but ask, "Have you trained like this before?"
"Something like that."
A few minutes later, Sergeant Quang said, "Alright, let's stop here. I'm soaked in sweat. System, end training."
The gravity swiftly returned to normal.
"This is a popular training area for those who want to improve their physiques," Sergeant Quang said as they walked out of the room.
They moved to the next training area afterward.
"This is the shooting range, where you can practice your aim. Though I doubt you'll need to train your aim anytime soon since you can shoot even better than many elite soldiers already."
"This is the sparring room. If you want to spice up your training by sparring with other soldiers, you can do so here."
"Have you ever tried Endless Assault in Gaia's Sanctum?" Sergeant Quang suddenly asked as they approached the 'Simulated Combat' room.
"I have," said Yuan.
"This room is exactly like that. The enemies and difficulty are the exact same, too."
"Oh? The exact same? How many floors or levels does it go up to?"
"Same as Endless Assault."
A smile tugged at Yuan's lips after hearing this, as this would allow him to fight the being on the 46th floor without needing to return to Gaia's Sanctum!
"There's no limit to how many times I can attempt a level, right?" Yuan asked, just to be sure.
"No. You can attempt it as many times as you like. Moreover, your record from Gaia's Sanctum is automatically transferred here, so you can start from whichever floor you reached there."
"Alright. I have decided. I am going to train here," Yuan declared.
"You don't have to wait for me since I won't be coming out anytime soon," he said to them.
"Even if you say that, we cannot abandon our duty." Sergeant Bing shook her head.
"Also, we have to stay here and make sure you come out in time for your mission," Sergeant Quang added.

chapters.title: Chapter 2596 First Mission in the Military
paragraphs: "Don't worry, I will definitely come out before then," Yuan assured them before entering the training room.
Inside was another hallway with multiple rooms.
A notification popped up the moment Yuan entered one of the available rooms.
<You will be teleported to the Simulated Training Area in 3 seconds>
After being teleported, Yuan found himself in a familiar area that resembled the waiting room in Gaia's Sanctum.
<Reading Player's Status>
<Transferring Player Status from Gaia's Sanctum>
<Transfer Successful>
<You can now challenge up to level 46>
Without hesitation, Yuan immediately challenged level 46.
<You will be teleported in 3 seconds>
Three seconds later, Yuan was teleported to the arena, where he reunited with the faceless entity that had dominated him during his time in Gaia's Sanctum.
"I'm back, you bastard," Yuan announced to the entity with a cold smile on his face.
"Foolish mortal!"
Just like it did in Gaia's Sanctum, the faceless entity spoke the same two words.
After acquiring his weapon of choice, a sword, Yuan immediately started fighting his opponent.
<Your restriction on Eternal Essence has been temporarily lifted>
However, to nobody's surprise, he died shortly afterward.
Yet, Yuan did not stop there and continued fighting it over and over again, just as he did in Gaia's Sanctum.
Time passed quickly, and in the blink of an eye, it was almost the start of a new week.

"Are you really worried about me?" Yuan suddenly said, breaking the silence.

"What?" Shi Fa frowned.
"Now that I am in the military, you can stop pretending not to know me."
"What is he talking about?" Sergeant Bing inquired with a curious yet puzzled face.
"This isn't our first time meeting," Yuan explained. "We met a few months ago at Gaia's Sanctum, and they even lost to me... in a two-versus-one."
"What?!" Sergeant Quang and Sergeant Bing exclaimed in shock.
Wu Wang rubbed his eyes and sighed out loud, "Did you really have to bring that up? It's not like we actually fought. We simply played a game of tag."
"Whether it was a real fight or not, both of you know what I am capable of better than anyone in the military right now, including General Mei." Yuan shrugged.
"Is that true?" Sergeant Bing asked the two.
"It's true..." Shi Fa sighed. "I won't go into details, but if anything happens out there, he'll likely be the safest out of all of us."
"However..." Wu Wang then spoke, "Just being able to survive won't be enough out there since our mission requires actual combat."
"So what? Do you want me to prove myself through a real fight with one of you or something?" Yuan asked.
Wu Wang and Shi Fa exchanged glances with each other.
After a moment of silence, Shi Fa said, "No... You can come with us. Even if you can't fight on the front lines, you can still support us from the rear with your shooting skills."
"You make it sound like we're going to be fighting dangerous monsters or something out there. Now I really cannot wait to go out there," Yuan remarked with an excited smile on his face.

chapters.title: Chapter 2597 The World Beyond the City Walls
paragraphs: "The General really didn't brief you on the mission, huh?" Wu Wang sighed after hearing Yuan's words.
"She said that she wanted to keep it a surprise." Yuan shrugged.
"I get that she's probably confident in our abilities, but this mission isn't a game..." Shi Fa shook his head.
"Anyway, let's talk about the mission itself," he continued. "For this mission, we are merely going to do a quick cleanup of the area around the city, which will take about a week or two at most."
"We will meet at the southern gates tomorrow at dawn. Any questions?"
Shi Fa turned to look at Yuan and asked, "Are you sure you don't have any questions?"
"I do, but I'll figure it out tomorrow," he said.
"Alright. In that case, see you all tomorrow."
Everyone returned to their living quarters shortly after.
"Do you intend to leave your living quarters again before the mission?" Sergeant Bing asked Yuan as they arrived at his living quarters.
"No."
"Then we'll leave you alone to pack for the mission. If you need to go anywhere, make sure to contact us."
"Pack? There are things to pack?"
"Oh, it's mostly just our weapons and personal luggage. Since you don't have a weapon, you don't have to worry about it. You can also bring anything you want."
"When you say weapons, do you mean Limitless Armaments?" Yuan asked in a curious tone.
"Yes."
"How does one acquire them? I also want one," he said.
"Only Sergeants and above can carry weapons," said Sergeant Bing.
"With that being said, you can try asking General Mei for one. She'll likely make an exception for you."
Yuan nodded.
"I'll ask her after the mission."
Some time later, Yuan entered his living quarters while Sergeant Bing and Sergeant Quang left to pack their things.
The following day, both of them returned to Yuan's living quarters and escorted him to the southern gate.
Unsurprisingly, Wu Wang and Shi Fa were already waiting for them when they arrived.
"Let's double-check our luggage before we head out," Sergeant Quang said.
Once they were done, they signed out at the gate.
"Teleport us to the city wall," Wu Wang said to the soldier on duty there.
"Yes, Sergeant!"
Moments later, the group stepped into the teleportation array and vanished from the military base, reappearing atop the city's towering wall.
"This is..." Yuan muttered in a dazed voice as he stared at the breathtaking scene before him.
Standing atop the massive wall at the city's edge, he was seeing the world beyond its borders for the very first time.

However, the sight was nothing like he had anticipated. Beyond the wall lay nothing but a barren wasteland, an endless expanse of sand and dirt stretching to the horizon like a scene from the apocalypse.
"What am I looking at?" Yuan asked out loud without turning away from the scenery, which was a stark contrast to the beautiful city that existed behind him.
"Quite the shocking sight, right? I remember my first time seeing the world beyond our city walls. I couldn't sleep properly for weeks on end," Wu Wang remarked.
"I didn't even know there was a city wall since I couldn't see it from my Sector," said Yuan.
He then asked, "What happened?
All four of them shrugged.
"Nobody knows for sure."
"What?" Yuan raised his eyebrows, dumbfounded by their response.
"How do you not know what caused such massive destruction?"
"Who said that was the cause?" Sergeant Bing said. "As far as we're aware, the world outside the city has always been like this."
"It's always been like this?" Yuan repeated in a low voice.
"Let's go." Shi Fa said before he suddenly leaped off the city wall and into the barren land.
Sergeant Quang and Wu Wang quickly followed.
"Follow us closely," Sergeant Bing said to Yuan before following the others.
The moment Yuan jumped off the city walls and exited the city's premises, the suppression on his cultivation was immediately released.
Meanwhile, Wu Wang retrieved his weapon, wielding it as though he was prepared to enter combat at any moment.
Sergeant Bing and Sergeant Quang both wielded a sword like Wu Wang, while Shi Fa wielded a spear.
"I don't see any enemies," Yuan said.
"You will soon," said Wu Wang.
They traveled for nearly half a day without encountering anything.
"Stop!"
Shi Fa suddenly came to a halt.
"Enemies ahead."
Yuan narrowed his eyes in the direction Shi Fa was looking, but he couldn't see anything, so he expanded the range of his divine sense.
"T-Those are...?!" Yuan's eyes widened in shock.
In the distance, several shadowy entities wandered aimlessly. Though their forms resembled humans, they appeared to possess no physical bodies, their entire beings composed of swirling black fog.
'Black Death?!' Yuan cried inwardly, as these entities resembled the Black Death he encountered when he was inside Vanishing Valley.
"We call them Void Specters because it's almost like you're staring into the void when you look at them," Shi Fa explained. "They don't have physical bodies and are immune to physical attacks."
"All they do is wander this barren land, as if they're constantly searching for something," Sergeant Quang continued.
"So our mission is to... kill them?" Yuan asked.
"Well... not exactly." Sergeant Bing shook her head. "These things are immortal. You can 'kill' them as many times as you want, but they will return a few weeks later as if nothing happened."
"Then why bother with them? Do they pose a threat to the city?"
"Not directly," Shi Fa explained. "When they get too close to the city, their presence interferes with our technology."
"That's why, before they get too close, we have to 'clean' them."
"Is that so..." Yuan mumbled.
"I know you're probably itching to fight them, but stay back for now," Wu Wang suddenly said. "We'll show you how it's done first."
"Sure." Yuan did not object.
Wu Wang and Shi Fa exchanged a glance.
Without a word, they nodded to each other before approaching the Void Specters.
"Hah!"
Their weapons surged with Limitless before they struck the Void Specters, slashing them in half without any resistance from the entities.
After being struck, the Void Specters dispersed like smoke, leaving behind a decent amount of Eternal Essence that lingered for a moment before disappearing as well.
Yuan raised an eyebrow at the sight.
'These things leave behind Eternal Essence when killed? I can probably train my Eternal Essence with this!' he immediately thought to himself.
However, the Eternal Essence disappeared after three seconds, so if he didn't immediately absorb them, it would vanish completely.
A few minutes later, Wu Wang and Shi Fa returned after clearing out all of the Void Specters.
"Is that it? That seemed a little too easy," Yuan remarked.
"For some reason, the closer they get to the city, the less aggressive they become," Shi Fa explained. "Once we venture farther out, they'll start fighting back."
"It still won't be too dangerous, but you can lose your life if you let your guard down, since they kill anything they touch," Wu Wang added.
"They don't have any long-range attacks, so you'll be relatively safe as long as you keep your distance," Sergeant Bing said. "The real danger lies in their numbers. You'll understand soon enough."
Shortly afterward, they continued venturing farther from the city.
A few minutes later, they encountered another Void Specter.

"You can take care of this one," Shi Fa said to Yuan. "Since you don't have a weapon, you can just shoot your Limitless at it. Though, it won't be as effective, and you might need to hit it a few times—"
Before Shi Fa could even finish his sentence, Yuan shot a single bullet of Limitless at the Void Specter.
Pop!
The moment the bullet reached the Void Specter, it exploded, instantly erasing the entity.
Shi Fa's mouth remained open for a good moment before he cleared his throat and spoke in a stiff voice, "Not bad, I guess."
<You have absorbed some Eternal Essence>
However, Yuan was focused on the notification that appeared after he absorbed the Eternal Essence the Void Specter left behind.
Although it wasn't much, it was better than nothing.
'At least I have a way to train my Eternal Essence now,' he smiled inwardly.
Not only that, but the others did not notice what he was doing. No, they were incapable of sensing Eternal Essence without the system, so there was no way for them to even know in the first place.
They continued their mission, eliminating every Void Specter they encountered. As they ventured farther from the city, the number of Void Specters steadily increased.
At first, they encountered only two or three at a time. Now, more than a dozen roamed within sight.
While the sergeants fought on the front lines, Yuan picked off the Void Specters from afar and absorbed the Eternal Essence they left behind.
Before long, he realized that their numbers weren't the only thing increasing. The Void Specters were also growing stronger and becoming increasingly difficult to kill.
However, that only meant Yuan needed two or three more bullets instead of just one to kill them.
Time flew by, and before they knew it, nearly a week had passed since they began their mission.
"All right, that should be enough cleaning for now," Shi Fa said. "Let's start heading back now."
"Huh? That's it? I want to clean up a little more," Yuan replied, dissatisfied that it was ending so soon.
"What? Why?" Wu Wang looked at him with a surprised expression.
"It's not like you'll gain bonus merit for going above and beyond for this sort of mission," he said a moment later, misunderstanding Yuan's intent.

chapters.title: Chapter 2598 Weapon of Choice
paragraphs: "Wu Wang's right. There's no point in staying out here longer than we need to. It's unnecessary risk," Shi Fa said.
"I have my own reason for wanting to continue cleaning up these Void Specters," Yuan said. "But we can head back for now."
"A reason to hunt Void Specters, huh? That's the first time I've heard such a thing," Sergeant Quang remarked. "Everyone I know considers this mission a punishment because of its nature."
"Then let's head back now. I want to wash myself as soon as possible," said Sergeant Bing.
They immediately started making their way back to the city.
As they traveled, Yuan asked, "How often do soldiers come out here to clean? And how are they picked?"
"Soldiers have to come out every other week for cleanup," Shi Fa replied. "As for who gets picked, there's a rotation, and it just happened to be our turn this week."
"In that case, when will it be our turn again?"
"We usually do this twice a year, so you can expect our next cleanup in half a year."
"Half a year? That's too long." Yuan frowned.
"Well, if you really want to, you can request to join the other squads for their cleanup," said Wu Wang.
"I can do that?"
"Sure..."
Wu Wang paused briefly before continuing, "Probably."
He shook his head and clarified, "Nobody has ever tried it before, so I can't really say for sure, but it's common to have additional soldiers or replacements for missions."
"I see. I will ask General Mei later."
"What is your reason for wanting to clean these Void Specters, anyway? They are literally just trash that needs to be cleaned every so often," Shi Fa asked.
"Trash that can kill you if you let them touch you..." Sergeant Bing added.
"It's a bit of a personal reason, so I'll keep it to myself for now," Yuan said.
"Is that so?"
Realizing that Yuan didn't want to talk about it, they stopped talking about the subject altogether.
Eventually, they returned to the city walls.
"Uh... are we going to have to climb this to return to the city?" Yuan asked as they stood at the very bottom of the towering walls.
"Unfortunately," Wu Wang sighed.
Without another word, all of them started flying to the top of the city walls.
Fortunately, they were still able to use their cultivation, allowing them to reach the top without any effort.
After reaching the top of the walls, they used the teleporter to return to the military base.
"It's my turn to do the report this week, so you guys can go ahead," Sergeant Quang said to them as they entered the military base.
"See you guys later."
Wu Wang and Shi Fa went their own ways after they reached the residential area.
"When are you going to meet with General Mei?" Sergeant Bing asked Yuan as she escorted him back to his living quarters.
"Tomorrow," he said.
"Alright. See you tomorrow. If you wish to go anywhere today, let either me or Sergeant Quang know."
"I won't go anywhere," he assured her.

"Pretty good.

"Well, I am not most soldiers," he replied with a smile.
"In fact, I want to talk to you about putting me on more of these missions."
"Excuse me?" Mei Feng muttered with raised eyebrows, wondering if she'd heard wrong.
"I want to keep doing these cleanup missions," he repeated in a slightly louder voice to ensure she heard him properly.
"This is a first," Mei Feng said after a moment of silence. "But just in case, you want to do the same mission, not a different one?"
"That's correct. I want to be sent outside the city to deal with the Void Specters," he said, making it as clear as possible so there was no way to misunderstand his desire.
"If that's what you really want..." Mei Feng nodded.
"How often do you want to do these missions?" she then asked.
"If possible, I would like you to put me on the next one."
"Huh? The next one?" Mei Feng raised her eyebrows.
"The next cleanup mission is scheduled to start in two days, but it'll be performed by another squad," she said.
"That's fine."
"No, it's not. In case you forgot, there are two soldiers currently protecting you. If I send you on a mission, they will have to come with you, so I won't just be sending a single soldier."

"Actually, I was going to talk to you about that," Yuan suddenly said. "I don't need any guards while I am outside the city since my cultivation isn't restricted out there, and I am more than capable of protecting myself."
"You—"

Mei Feng opened her mouth to speak, but Yuan interrupted, "I understand that you're only looking out for me, but I don't need a babysitter everywhere I go. If you don't think I can protect myself out there, I am more than willing to prove myself."
Mei Feng fell silent, her eyes narrowing as she pondered his words.
Eventually, she spoke, "If that's what you want, I have no obligation to refuse. However, if anything happens while you are outside, you'll have nobody but yourself to blame."
Yuan nodded.
"Thank you, General."
"Then I will add you to the next cleanup mission and notify the soldiers doing it. Anything else?"
"One more thing. Do you think it's possible for me to carry a weapon?" Yuan then asked.
"A weapon, huh? Normally, only Sergeants are allowed to carry them, but since you're already doing missions..."
Mei Feng spent another moment pondering before giving a response, "Alright, I'll approve of it. You can visit the armory after this and request a weapon."
"I will."
"If there's nothing else, you can leave."
Yuan left the room shortly after.

"I guess the General agreed to let you carry a weapon," he said with a smile.
"Not only that, but she agreed to let me go on the next cleanup mission, which will happen two days from now."
"Huh? That means we'll also have to—"
"No, you don't have to come with me," Yuan quickly interrupted. "I've told the General that I don't need any bodyguards while I am outside since I am more than capable of protecting myself."
"Are you sure?"
"I am."
"As long as you're sure—not that I am complaining, since this means more free time for me."
They arrived at the armory half an hour later.
"This is the armory. Just approach any of the available counters and tell them you're here to receive your weapon," Sergeant Quang said to him.
Yuan followed his instructions and approached one of the counters.
"I'm here to receive my weapon."
The man working behind the counter gestured at the machine on the table between them.
A moment later, Yuan's information appeared for the man to see.
The first thing that came up was Yuan's rank, and when the man saw this, he immediately frowned.
"Listen here, Corporal—"
However, he suddenly stopped midway when he noticed that despite being a Corporal, Yuan had permission to carry a weapon.
'A Corporal with a weapon? Who gave him the permission?'
Out of curiosity, the man checked the individual who signed off on it.
"General Mei?!" he exclaimed in shock after seeing her name.
After snapping out of his daze, the man turned to look at Yuan and swallowed nervously before speaking, "W-What kind of weapon are you looking to carry, Corporal Yuan?"
Yuan did not immediately respond.
Before arriving, he'd already decided to pick what he was used to the most—a sword. However, now that he was moments away from receiving his weapon, he suddenly had an urge to use a different weapon.
"You got guns?" he asked.
"Of course, we do. What kind of gun do you want?"
"Whatever lets me shoot the fastest."
"That would be a minigun, but this kind of weapon is only really used for training since it exhausts your Limitless insanely rapidly, and most people run out of Limitless in a few seconds."
"I want it," Yuan quickly said.
"You want... the minigun?" The man asked just in case he heard wrong.
"I do."
"Uh... sure...? Give me a moment..."
The man disappeared into a room at the back before returning with a minigun nearly as large as he was.
"Here you go."
"Thanks," Yuan said, casually holding the minigun with one hand.
"There's no way you actually picked that as your weapon..." Sergeant Bing remarked with a dumbfounded face when Yuan returned to them with his new weapon.
"What are you thinking, picking that weapon?" Sergeant Quang shook his head. "Fortunately, you can change your weapon at any time."
"I wanted something that would help me clean up the Void Specters as fast and efficiently as possible," Yuan explained.
"While I can't deny the minigun can do that, you'll run out of energy in a matter of seconds," said Sergeant Bing.
"I should be fine," Yuan responded with a confident smile.
After a moment of silence, Sergeant Quang sighed, "I know you said you don't need a bodyguard outside the city, but I am going to follow you anyway."
"Me too," said Sergeant Bing. "Not only am I concerned, but I am also curious."
"If that's what you want."
Yuan nodded, not refusing their company since it was their own decision to follow him.

"Are you not even going to try it out before bringing it with you on the mission?" Sergeant Bing questioned him.
"No need," he said.
"Is that so..."
"Then we'll see you in two days. If you need to go anywhere, you know where to find us."
Sergeant Bing and Sergeant Quang left shortly after, returning to their own living quarters that were only a few steps away from Yuan's residence.
Yuan remained at home the entire time, and in the blink of an eye, it was time for the mission.
At the eastern gates, four soldiers were standing around, seemingly waiting for someone.
"What are we waiting for?"
"I just learned of this last night, but we'll have an extra for this mission." The Squad Leader explained.
"Really? Who?"
"I wasn't given any details except that it's some Corporal."
"Huh? A Corporal? For cleanup duty? It must be punishment."
"Even if it's punishment, it seems a bit harsh."
"A punishment for them or us? Since it's a Corporal, they won't have a weapon, which will make cleanup a lot more difficult."
"We can just make them carry our luggage or something," one of them suggested.
A few moments later, they noticed three figures approaching them.
"Hm? Sergeant Bing? Sergeant Quang? Are you also going out for a mission today?"
The soldiers recognized them and asked.
"Yes, we'll be joining you on your cleanup mission."
"What?"
The soldiers exchanged puzzled glances with each other.
"W-Wait a second... I was told that it would only be a single individual, and that they were a Corporal," said the Squad Leader.
"That would be me," Yuan finally spoke up. "They decided to join me. That won't be a problem, right?"
The soldiers raised their eyebrows when they saw Yuan and the large weapon he was carrying.
"Is that... a minigun?" one of them asked, sounding incredulous.
"Sure is."
"I won't question why a Corporal has a weapon, but do you plan on going outside with that?"
"Of course. Why else would I bring it? For emotional support?" Yuan responded sarcastically.
The group fell silent, and they turned to look at Sergeant Bing and Sergeant Quang with frowns.
"Ahem..." Sergeant Bing awkwardly cleared her throat before speaking, "You guys don't need to concern yourself with him. We're here for that reason."
A moment later, the squad leader said, "Since everyone's here, let's head out."
Shortly afterward, they teleported to the city walls and departed from there.

Just like on Yuan's first mission, they encountered barely any Void Specters during the first several hours. However, as they ventured farther from the city walls, the number of Void Specters gradually increased.
When there were only a few Void Specters, the original group for the mission did all of the work while Yuan and his group quietly followed behind.
Of course, it wasn't as if Yuan did absolutely nothing, as he had to absorb all of the Eternal Essence left behind by the Void Specters.

The others didn't blame Yuan for standing back, either. As ridiculous as Yuan's weapon was in their eyes, they understood that its outrageous energy consumption prevented him from using it recklessly.
"So, when are you actually going to use that thing?" Sergeant Bing eventually asked Yuan.
"I followed you out here because I wanted to see how quickly you regret picking it as your weapon."
Yuan chuckled and calmly replied, "Why didn't you say so earlier?"
After the original group finished cleaning up the Void Specters, Yuan said to them, "You guys can sit back from this point forward. I'll take care of things from here on out."
"What are you talking about?" They muttered, looking confused.
Yuan held his minigun before his chest and said, "I've been itching to use this."
After a moment of silence, their squad leader said, "Do as you please."
None of them objected, as they had no reason to stop Yuan, after all.
Some time later, when they encountered more Void Specters, the squad leader gestured at them while looking directly at Yuan.
"All yours," he said.
Yuan did not respond and quietly raised his weapon, pointing its muzzles in the direction of the oblivious Void Specters.
He gathered his Limitless and poured it into the minigun. Then, without warning, started shooting a barrage of bullets at the Void Specters.
Whoosh!
The bullets tore through the air, riddling the group of twenty or so Void Specters with dozens of holes and annihilating them in the blink of an eye.
Despite the spectacular display, none of the soldiers reacted. They remained completely nonchalant, as though they had witnessed the same scene countless times before.
Shortly afterward, they continued onward, and Yuan dealt with every Void Specter that appeared along the way.
Although everything seemed normal at first, and none of the soldiers reacted to Yuan's performance, they eventually began to sense something was off.
"Hey... how long has it been since he took our place?"
"About twelve hours. Why?"
"Don't you find it odd...?"
"What do you mean?"
"He's using a minigun, you know? A weapon notorious for exhausting its user within a few hours, even when fired sparingly. Yet he's been shooting nonstop for twelve hours!"
"Holy shit! You're right! How the hell is he still able to shoot that thing?! That's some insane stamina!"
The others reacted with shock after realizing this anomaly.
"It's not just his stamina." Sergeant Quang suddenly said. "If you didn't notice, it only takes him four to five bullets at most to defeat a Void Specter, which typically takes over a dozen."
The soldiers swallowed nervously when they realized what Sergeant Quang was trying to say.
Not only was Yuan not exhausted after using the minigun for so long without a break, but he was even using more power than normal!
"Who the hell is he?"
The squad leader asked.
"Corporal Yuan, a prodigy who joined the military not even a month ago," said Sergeant Bing.
"Excuse me?!"
The soldiers exclaimed in shock and disbelief.

chapters.title: Chapter 2600 Five Zones
paragraphs: "It hasn't been a month since he joined the military?! And he's already a Corporal?! Do you really expect me to believe that?!"
"He was promoted to Corporal right after the recruitment due to his performance, which broke all of the previous records," said Sergeant Quang.

"I heard rumors of a monster with talents on par with the Ironwoman appearing in the recent recruitment... Are you telling me that individual is him?" The squad leader swallowed nervously at this realization.
"Of course. Why else would we, Sergeants, be accompanying a Corporal like him?" Sergeant Bing remarked.
"I thought you were friends..."
"Nope. He is under our protection... by General Mei's orders." Sergeant Quang revealed.
The soldiers turned to look at Yuan with dazed expressions, seeing him in a new light.
Over the next several days, Yuan single-handedly eliminated every Void Specter they encountered.

Because he was clearing them so quickly, the squad traveled much farther than originally planned. In fact, they didn't realize how far they'd ventured until they began encountering Void Specters that were noticeably larger than the ones they'd seen before.
Not only did the Void Specters become more durable as they ventured further away from the city, but they also grew larger in size.
Of course, this also meant that the amount of Eternal Essence they left behind increased.
"Hey, I know you're having fun, but it's time to start heading back. There's no point cleaning more than we should... and we've already gone overboard."
"Can we stay for two... no, one more day?" Yuan asked.
"What are we, at the amusement park...?" The squad leader remarked while shaking his head.
"What are you trying to achieve by staying longer?" asked another soldier.
"He has a personal reason for wanting to clear the Void Specters," Sergeant Bing answered for him.
"He volunteered to participate in this mission for a reason," Sergeant Quang added.
"What did you say? He volunteered for this mission?"
The soldiers looked at him with wide eyes.
"I thought he was being punished."
"Nope."
"Well, whatever his reason is, it's too dangerous to go further than this," said the squad leader. "Hell, we've already entered the Orange Zone."
"Orange Zone? What's that?" Yuan asked, as this was his first time hearing such a term.
The squad leader was prepared to mock Yuan for not knowing such basic knowledge, but quickly recalled that Yuan had just joined the military and held himself back.

"The world outside the city is divided into five zones, with each color representing a different danger level. The Green Zone is closest to the city, followed by the Orange Zone. Beyond that are the Red, Purple, and Black Zones. Cleanup missions typically remain within the Green Zone," he explained.
"What makes each zone different besides the Void Specters becoming larger and harder to kill?" Yuan asked.

"The Void Specters don't just become harder to kill," Sergeant Quang explained. "In the Orange Zone, they begin fighting back. In the Red Zone and beyond, they become aggressive and actively hunt anyone who enters."
"Then what sort of mission requires one to traverse so far away from the city?" Yuan continued to ask.
"That's..." The soldiers immediately looked hesitant to tell him for some reason.
"Let me guess... You can't tell me because of my rank?" Yuan speculated.
"That's right."
They admitted.
"Then forget it," said Yuan a moment later. "Anyways, we can start heading back now."
Thus, they started heading back to the city.
As they traveled, Yuan received a notification.
<You have received some merit for clearing a mission>
<Your credential has increased slightly>
'Since I am technically still in the middle of my second mission, this must be for my first one,' Yuan thought to himself, thinking that it took rather long for him to receive credit for the mission.
After returning to the city, Yuan and the other group parted ways.
"Do you even feel tired in the slightest?" Sergeant Bing asked Yuan as they made their way back to their residence.
"No," he answered.
"No wonder you picked the minigun as your weapon... You have opened my eyes," she said.
"Hey, I have been wondering... is it possible to go outside the city by myself?" Yuan suddenly asked.
"You want to do cleanup missions by yourself...?" Sergeant Quang immediately guessed his thoughts.
Yuan nodded.
"I don't know, and you're definitely asking the wrong people."
"Guess I'll go speak with General Mei again."
